experiment_name: Meno-J Experiment 6: P4-F1 Score and Conditioning Comparison Across Sample Sizes
prior_result: Experiment 5 / P4-F2 falsified the broad finite-sample-only explanation.

simulation_config.region_conditioning_scope: Observable generator-defined region/subgroup; unseen test regions receive an infinite conservative threshold.
simulation_config.persistent_failure_rule: mean coverage_gap > 0.15 OR mean minimum_group_coverage < 0.75 at n=600

roadmap_entry.title: Nonconformity Score and Conditioning Strategy Comparison Across Sample Sizes
roadmap_entry.failure_condition_for_working_theory: If the performance ranking of nonconformity scores/conditioning strategies reverses as calibration size increases (i.e., margin scores win at small n, Mahalanobis wins at large n), the working theory that structural mismatch is primary is falsified.

experiment_design.title: Nonconformity Score and Conditioning Strategy Comparison Across Sample Sizes
experiment_design.design: Using a large multi-subject wearable stress dataset (e.g., WESAD, N>1000 subjects), subsample calibration sets of varying sizes (n=50, 100, 500, 1000, 5000). For each size, evaluate a grid of nonconformity scores (softmax margin, Mahalanobis distance, conformalized quantile regression) and conditioning strategies (marginal, Mondrian with reactivity strata, block-conformal with transition phases, MAI bins, mixture-model clusters). Measure coverage and interval width on a fixed large test set. Plot coverage vs. calibration size for each combination. Test whether performance ranking changes with sample size (indicating variance-dominated) or remains stable (indicating bias-dominated).
experiment_design.meno_j_prediction: Mahalanobis and mixture-model conditioning achieve nominal coverage at smaller sample sizes (n=500) and maintain advantage at all sizes; margin scores and fixed bins require larger n to reach nominal coverage. The ranking is stable, indicating structural alignment.
experiment_design.competing_explanation_prediction: At small n, margin scores and coarse conditioning win due to lower variance; at large n, Mahalanobis and fine conditioning win. The crossover point identifies the variance-bias tradeoff, not fundamental geometry.
measurable_outcomes: Coverage probability vs. calibration set size for each score/strategy
Variance of coverage estimates across bootstrap resamples

expected_effect_size.metric: Calibration sample size needed to achieve 95% coverage (±1%)
expected_effect_size.expected_direction: Working theory: Mahalanobis/mixture-model need ~500 samples; margin/fixed bins need ~5000. Competitor: crossover at ~2000 samples.
expected_effect_size.quantitative_target: ≥2x difference in required sample size between best and worst strategy at nominal coverage; stability of ranking across sizes.
expected_effect_size.rationale: H6, H7, H8 suggest medium effect sizes for score/strategy choice; sample size effects are well-known in conformal literature.

required_datasets_or_metadata: Large multi-subject wearable stress dataset with multimodal features (ECG, EDA, respiration, accelerometer)
Implementations of all nonconformity scores and conditioning strategies
Computational resources for extensive subsampling experiments
experiment_design.difficulty_reason: Computational experiment on existing data; no new data collection needed.
experiment_design.failure_condition_for_working_theory: If the performance ranking of nonconformity scores/conditioning strategies reverses as calibration size increases (i.e., margin scores win at small n, Mahalanobis wins at large n), the working theory that structural mismatch is primary is falsified.
experiment_design.score_rationale: High feasibility, good information gain; uses existing data; relevant to methodological practice.

experiment_5_source.strongest_failure_case: sparse_subgroup_geometry / inverse_probability_score / marginal: mean n=300 coverage gap 0.7462, mean minimum group coverage 0.1538.

core_answers.calibration_size_effect: Increasing n_calib resolved 0 of 13 cells that met the failure threshold at n=50; 15 cells still failed at n=600. Mean gap changed from 0.2119 to 0.2222.

p4_followup_assessment.rationale: 15 of 45 score-conditioning-geometry cells retained a gap above 0.15 or minimum group coverage below 0.75 at n_calib=600.
p4_followup_assessment.strongest_structural_failure_case: sparse_subgroup_geometry / inverse_probability_score / marginal: n=600 mean gap 0.7591, minimum group coverage 0.1409.
p4_followup_assessment.strongest_size_effect_case: overlapping_gaussian_clusters / margin_score / mondrian_class: gap fell from 0.1128 to 0.0286 (reduction 0.0842).

limitations: The classifier is regularized LDA rather than a deep wearable stress detector.
Region labels are generator-defined and observable, not estimated from noisy embeddings.
An unseen test region receives an infinite threshold, guaranteeing conservative but potentially uninformative sets.
Five seeds quantify common Monte Carlo variation but not extremely rare tails.
Synthetic Gaussian geometry does not reproduce all temporal and sensor-quality effects in wearable data.
next_recommended_experiment: Apply the safest and most dangerous score-conditioning pairs to a real multi-subject wearable benchmark with subject, activity, sensor-quality, and time-segment metadata.
